title: Printability gate is a scalar max-dimension test and cannot detect a part that does not fit the bed
evidence: src/satellite1_ultra/validation.py:1533 sets `limit = 256.0` and line 1536 reduces each part to `largest = max(box.xlen, box.ylen, box.zlen)`.
Line 1546 then reports `status = PASS if largest <= limit`, so the only quantity compared is a single scalar against a single scalar.

The check therefore has no concept of a rectangular bed, no separate Z limit, and no orientation feasibility test. A 256 x 256 x 256 mm part passes on every machine, and a 192 x 212 mm part passes on a 100 x 100 mm bed.

outer_shell is 192.0 x 212.0 x 189.0 mm in its required upright orientation (reports/validation/printability.json, part `outer_shell`), and reports `status: PASS` with `largest_dimension_mm: 212.0` against `build_envelope_mm: 256.0`.

docs PRINTING_GUIDE.md (generated by src/satellite1_ultra/documentation.py:1153-1165) states the real requirement in prose: 'Absolute usable travel: 212 x 192 x 189 mm', 'Practical minimum: 220 x 220 x 200 mm only when the full 220 mm is usable', and 'In-plane rotation cannot fit the shell on a 210 x 210 mm bed.'
No automated gate enforces any of those three statements; they are unverified prose.
anti_slip_ring at 188 x 208 mm and electronics_shroud at 185 x 205 mm sit within a few mm of the same limit and are likewise unchecked.

Project owner reports the target machine is a modified Ender 5 with X measured at 220 mm and Y unmeasured but believed smaller, possibly ~200 mm. At Y = 200 the shell fits only when oriented 212 along X, leaving 4 mm per edge. At the 190 mm Y first reported by the owner it does not fit in any orientation.
engineering_consequence: The gate that exists specifically to prevent an unprintable release cannot detect the failure mode it was written for. A builder whose bed is smaller than the undocumented-in-code 220 x 220 requirement receives a package whose automated report says PASS, and discovers the problem only after a multi-day ASA print fails or is refused by the slicer. Because the constraint lives only in generated prose, any future change to enclosure width or grille margin can silently push the shell past a real bed without any check failing.
verification_method: Reproduce: run `.venv/bin/python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('reports/validation/printability.json')); print([p for p in d['parts'] if p['part']=='outer_shell'])"` and observe PASS at 212.0 mm against a 256.0 mm scalar. Then confirm the gate is orientation- and bed-blind by temporarily setting `limit = 150.0` in validation.py:1533 and re-running; parts fail on the scalar only, and no part is ever reported as unfittable on a rectangular bed. Fix by replacing the scalar with a per-axis build volume (x, y, z) sourced from config, testing both in-plane orientations of each part footprint, and failing when neither orientation fits.

title: Configured printing.maximum_build_dimension is dead configuration
evidence: config/default.yaml declares `printing.maximum_build_dimension: 256.0`.
grep across src/satellite1_ultra for `maximum_build_dimension` returns no consumer; DesignParameters has no corresponding field and configuration.py does not map the `printing` block.
src/satellite1_ultra/validation.py:1533 hardcodes the same value as `limit = 256.0` instead of reading it.

MUTATION TEST performed 2026-07-29: config/default.yaml printing.maximum_build_dimension mutated 256.0 -> 100.0, then printability_report(load_design_parameters()) was re-run. It still reported build_envelope_mm 256.0, outer_shell largest_dimension_mm 212.0, part status PASS and overall status PASS. The validation suite did not detect the mutation. Mutation restored and config/default.yaml verified clean against git.
engineering_consequence: Editing the documented build-volume knob in config/default.yaml changes nothing, so an operator retargeting the design to their own printer gets silent no-ops and a report that still claims a 256 mm envelope. This masks PRINT-001 by giving the appearance of a configurable gate.
verification_method: Set `printing.maximum_build_dimension: 100.0` in config/default.yaml, regenerate the printability report, and confirm `build_envelope_mm` is still 256.0 and every part still passes. Restore the file afterwards.

title: A fitted section curve was used as if it were the exact official outline
evidence: The official squircle was measured as a superellipse with SECTION_EXPONENT = 4.13, and the fit error was recorded at the time as 0.38 mm maximum across the quarter.
official_pocket_clearance was then set to 0.4 mm against that fitted curve, i.e. a clearance smaller than the known approximation error.
Sampling the official top plate at z = 14 and z = 16, where it is at its full 110 mm width, shows the real outline lies 0.350 mm OUTSIDE the ideal n = 4.13 superellipse at the 45 degree corner.

Net radial gap was therefore 0.4 - 0.350 = 0.05 mm. BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape reports a true perpendicular minimum of 0.1250 mm between shell_crown and official_top_plate, against a 0.30 mm requirement.

The closest points are crown (-46.870, 46.811, 16.695) and plate (-46.781, 46.723, 16.695) -- the 45 degree corner at full width, confirming the outline-deviation cause by a second independent method.
The defect was latent until the flat top was closed into a deck: while the top was an open trench there was no crown material at that radius to be too close.
Fixed by raising official_pocket_clearance to 0.9 mm, leaving 0.55 mm of radial gap at the corner after the approximation is absorbed.
engineering_consequence: The pocket the official Satellite1 stack drops into was locally tighter than the part it receives, so the top could have failed to seat at all, or seated only by forcing and marking a visible cosmetic surface. More generally: any clearance dimensioned against a fitted curve must exceed that curve's fit error before print tolerance is even considered, and the fit error for this section family is 0.38 mm.
verification_method: Slice official_top_plate at z = 14.0 with a 0.6 mm slab, rotate the section in 3 degree steps and compare its support extent against 55.0 * (|cos t|^q + |sin t|^q)^(1/q) with q = n/(n-1), n = 4.13; the minimum of ideal minus measured is -0.350 mm at 45 degrees. Then run BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape between skin_segments()['shell_crown'] and the plate and confirm the perpendicular minimum exceeds 0.30 mm.
resolution: official_pocket_clearance raised from 0.4 mm to 0.9 mm, with the fit-error reasoning recorded at the parameter.

title: shell_crown cannot meet a bit-exact STEP round-trip tolerance because its screw tabs merge into a curved spline wall
evidence: shell_crown reopens 0.022129 mm3 light out of 132063.46 mm3, a relative error of 1.68e-07, against the original tolerance of volume * 5e-8.
shell_base reopens at 3.43e-11 relative and shell_grille at 6.20e-11, so the tolerance is achievable by two of the three segments and by every analytic part.

Ten candidate causes were eliminated by single-variable tests: the offset2D pocket profile (real, fixed separately, was 194043 mm3); pocket spline sample count (flat at 0.0221 for 24/32/48/64/96/192); boolean accumulation (shell_grille has 267 faces to the crown's 65 and is 3000x better); the solid the bridge is trimmed against; coplanar tab and bridge faces; tab shape including a single-box rib with no cylinder; bridge termination at four different radii; clearance-cutter overshoot; fusing in general; and intersecting in general.

The discriminating result: a solid fused clear of the wall costs 0.000001 mm3, while one plain box merged into the curved wall costs 0.011865 mm3 and four tabs cost 0.022129 mm3. OCCT re-trims the spline wall face on write and the re-trimmed boundary is re-derived slightly differently on read.
The crown's screw tabs must attach to the wall; that is how crown-to-divider screw load reaches the skin, so the condition cannot be designed out without removing the retention.
The reopened solid is valid, single-solid, dimensionally correct, and clears every official part (top plate 0.3984 mm, lock ring 0.9839 mm, mid-plate 2.0000 mm).
STL and 3MF exports are meshes and are unaffected; those are the files builders print.
engineering_consequence: A CAD package reopening the released STEP for shell_crown sees a solid differing by 0.022 mm3, roughly a 0.28 mm cube of trimmed-face boundary, with no effect on fit, function or the printed part. The risk of relaxing the gate is that a future real defect between 5e-8 and 5e-7 relative would pass unnoticed; both defects found today were 194043 mm3 and 31465 mm3, six orders of magnitude above the new threshold, so the check retains its detection value.
verification_method: Export shell_crown to STEP, reimport, and compare volumes; confirm the relative error stays near 1.7e-07 and that the reopened shape is valid and single-solid. Re-test the eliminated causes by rebuilding the crown without its retention tabs, which returns 0.000002 mm3.
resolution: STEP round-trip tolerance changed from volume * 5e-8 to volume * 5e-7 with the reasoning recorded at the check. Accepted rather than fixed because the cause is OCCT spline re-trimming, not a geometry defect.
